c74object.name: evi_lfo
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_lfo.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_lfo.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
The evi_lfo.genexpr file also requires:
evi_sources.genexpr
About this File:
A collection of computed but efficient LFOs

entry.name: lfoMix ( )
entry.description:
A computed but cheap LFO that can morph between triangle and sine shapes, requires phase 0..1 input, produces wave shape output in range 0..1
In 1: type=input: phase, Phase 0..1
In 2: type=input: duty, Duty of triangle wave, 0..1, 0.5==tri
In 3: type=input: shape, Morph between tri..sine 0..1
In 4: type=input: skew, Skew exponent of LFO output, 0.5..2, 1==no skew
Return 1: LFO, Wave output in range 0..1

entry.name: lfoSkew ( )
entry.description:
A cheap computed simple sine lfo with added skew, phase 0..1 in, wave 0..1 out
In 1: type=input: phase, Phase 0..1
In 2: type=input: skew, Skew exponent of LFO output, 0.5..2, 1==no skew
Return 1: LFO, Wave output in range 0..1

entry.name: lfoShapes01 ( )
entry.description:
Collection of computed switchable LFOs, all wave selections in output range 0..1
In 1: type=input: phase, Phase 0..1
In 2: type=input: sync, The sync of the phase input required for random LFOs
In 3: type=input: width, Pulse width input 0..1 for LFOs that require it (3=tri, 5=tanh, 6=square)
In 4: type=input: wave, 0=bypass, 1=ramp up, 2=ramp down, 3=tri, 4=sine (default), 5=tanh, 6=square, 7=rand step, 8=rand linear, 9=rand cubic, 10=noise
Return 1: LFO, Selected LFO wave in range 0..1

entry.name: lfoShapes11 ( )
entry.description:
Collection of computed switchable LFOs, all wave selections in output range -1..1
In 1: type=input: phase, Phase 0..1
In 2: type=input: sync, The sync of the phase input required for random LFOs
In 3: type=input: width, Pulse width input 0..1 for LFOs that require it (3=tri, 5=tanh, 6=square)
In 4: type=input: wave, 0=bypass, 1=ramp up, 2=ramp down, 3=tri, 4=sine (default), 5=tanh, 6=square, 7=rand step, 8=rand linear, 9=rand cubic, 10=noise
Return 1: LFO, Selected LFO wave in range -1..1
